answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The ember multiplier is published, charged in knoll, and ledge lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1632 identities would post 2806 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
